# Feature Inventory → Research Model Mapping

> Reconstructed from the architecture we settled on (SBM + GNN + RNN + Bayesian network
> for Paper 1; NRB-shock econometric causal design for Paper 2), not quoted verbatim from
> the earlier model spec — check against what we specifically fixed earlier if anything
> looks off.

## Feature inventory (what the parser extracts, per BFI per month)

**Balance sheet** — stock variables: `CAPITAL FUND` (+ paid-up capital, reserves, retained
earnings), `BORROWINGS` split by counterparty (**NRB**, **interbank borrowing**, foreign
banks, other financial ins., bonds), `DEPOSITS` (current/savings/fixed/call × domestic/
foreign), `LOANS & ADVANCES`, `LIQUID FUNDS`, `INVESTMENT IN SECURITIES`,
`SHARE & OTHER INVESTMENT` (incl. **interbank lending**), `FIXED/OTHER ASSETS`,
`TOTAL ASSETS` / `TOTAL Liabilities`.

**P&L** — flow variables: `Interest Expense` / `Interest Income` (each broken out by
deposit type / investment type), `Commission`, `Staff Expense`, `Provision for Risk`
(loan-loss provisioning, general/specific/watch-list), `Loan Written Off`, `Net Profit`,
`Total Expenses`.

**Statement of credit** — composition variables: sector-wise loan shares (12 sectors incl.
agriculture, construction, real estate, tourism...), product-wise shares (term loan,
overdraft, real estate loan, consumption loan...), collateral-wise shares (guarantee type,
property, securities).

## Mapping to Paper 1 (network reconstruction: SBM / GNN / RNN / Bayesian net)

| Model slot | NRB field(s) | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **Node features x_i,t** (GNN input) | `TOTAL ASSETS` (size), `CAPITAL FUND` (capital), `DEPOSITS`+`BORROWINGS` (funding mix), `LOANS & ADVANCES`+`INVESTMENT IN SECURITIES` (asset mix) | Per-bank attribute vector at each GNN layer / RNN timestep |
| **Temporal panel** (RNN input) | Same node features indexed by `year_bs`/`month_bs` | This dataset *is* the monthly panel — no extra work needed once the archive is batch-extracted |
| **Edge-reconstruction margins (SBM / entropy method)** | **`b. Interbank Borrowing`** (liability-side row sum) + **`a. Interbank Lending`** (asset-side column sum) | This is the actual payoff: NRB never publishes the bilateral interbank matrix, only these two marginal totals per bank. That's exactly the input the classic network-reconstruction literature (maximum-entropy / SBM-regularized) needs to infer the latent bilateral exposure matrix — this dataset is a direct fit for Paper 1's stated method, not just a proxy. |
| **Block/community prior (SBM)** | BFI class (A/B/C, from the aggregate summary pages) + size | Stochastic block prior over bank "types" before refining with GNN embeddings |
| **Bayesian-net structural constraints** | `TOTAL ASSETS = TOTAL Liabilities`; `Total Expenses + Net Profit = Total Income`; `CAPITAL FUND = Σ(sub-items a–g)` | Known accounting identities — fix these as deterministic edges in the DAG rather than letting the model "discover" them, which regularizes the learned structure and gives a built-in correctness check |
| **Common-exposure / contagion channel** | Sector-wise and product-wise credit shares | Two banks both concentrated in, say, real estate are correlated through a shared shock even with zero direct interbank linkage — a second edge-formation signal independent of the interbank margins above |

## Mapping to Paper 2 (NRB regulatory-shock causal design)

| Model slot | NRB field(s) | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **Treatment** | *Not in this dataset* — needs a separate NRB circular/directive date series (CRR change, provisioning rule, rate corridor) | External to the parser; still needs sourcing |
| **Outcome Y** | `Net Profit`, `Provision for Risk`, `LOANS & ADVANCES` growth, sector credit growth, interest margin (`Interest Income` − `Interest Expense`) | Candidate dependent variables |
| **Controls** | `CAPITAL FUND / TOTAL ASSETS` (capital adequacy proxy), `LIQUID FUNDS / DEPOSITS` (liquidity ratio), log `TOTAL ASSETS` (size), BFI class dummy | Standard bank-level covariates |
| **Spillover regressor — the link back to Paper 1** | Σⱼ (reconstructed interbank weight wᵢⱼ from Paper 1) × (1 if bank *j* directly shocked) | This is the actual bridge between the two papers: Paper 1's reconstructed network isn't just a standalone contribution, it's the mechanism that lets Paper 2 identify *indirect* (network-propagated) treatment effects on banks not directly targeted by the regulation — otherwise Paper 2 is just a standard panel diff-in-diff with no network story. |

## Known gap

`item_code` (the "4", "a.", "1.1.2.1" hierarchy) only exists on balance sheet/P&L. If any
model component wants a consistent parent-child line-item taxonomy across all three
statements (e.g., for automated feature aggregation across years where wording drifts),
the credit statement will need category labels matched by string, not code, since it has
no numbering in the source document.
